To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the assembly of M band titins, M-protein, and myomesin is a highly coordinated process that proceeds at a much higher rate in vitro than in vivo.

(1) titin, myofibers (myomesin) and M-protein are incorporated into the M band region at different times, (2) M-protein expression is variable in cultured myofibers, (3) the M band epitopes of titin are not accessible during earlier developmental stages, and (4) sarcomere assembly is much faster in vitro than in vivo.
(1) M band epitopes of titin are not accessible in non-striating myofibrils and (2) M-protein expression varies among myotubes derived from different muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of the M band region in differentiating myotubes.
the molecular organization of the sarcomeres and the mechanisms involved in the formation of the M band during in vitro myogenesis of human skeletal muscle.
the molecular events of sarcomere assembly and their regulation in human skeletal muscle cells during in vitro myogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M band titin, myosin and myomesin appear to be assembled in a sequential manner during in vitro myofibrilogenesis.

the assembly of titin, and myomesin and the incorporation of M protein into the sarcomere M band region is a very late event during myofibrilogenesis, and that the incorporation of M band proteins seems to be a highly regulated process.
M band titin epitope expression and myomesin incorporation in the sarcomeric lattice are early events, while M-protein expression and binding to the M band is delayed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of M band epitopes into sarcomeric positions is not an early event in myofibril assembly.
the assembly of the M band region in differentiating myofibers is a highly organized process that requires the sequential incorporation of titin, followed by myomesin and finally M-protein.

the incorporation of M band proteins into nascent myofibers occurs in a highly ordered and coordinated fashion, and that the assembly of this part of the M band region is a late event in myofibrilogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibodies against M band titin are valuable tools in studies of the assembly of the M band region.
the assembly of the titin, myomosin and M-proteins into the M band region of the sarcomeres in human skeletal muscle cells is a highly organized process.
the assembly of the M band is an ordered process that requires the simultaneous presence of titin and the myomesin/M-protein complex.
